title.en: Analytics Products: Semantic Layers and Conversational Analytics
title.ar: منتجات التحليلات: الطبقات الدلالية والتحليلات الحوارية

tagline: Define metrics once as tested code, serve them through a governed semantic layer, and let an assistant answer only the questions it has proved it can answer
description: Participants build the analytics product of the fictional Qamar Telecom, whose 300 managers want to ask questions in Arabic and English about usage, billing, collections and complaints. They define metrics once as tested code with owners, design a semantic layer with conformed time, tariff history and access rules by region and classification, expose it to tools and agents, and evaluate a conversational assistant on certified questions, ending with a policy on which questions the assistant may answer. DS-307 covers single-area metrics, dashboards and a first agent test; this course designs the layer across business areas and governs the assistant.
audience: Specialists. Data scientists who have completed the level 300 core and practicum, or can show equivalent work: an analysis they led from question to recommendation and defended.
prerequisites: DS-307 Metrics, Semantic Models and Dashboards
Writes SQL over a star schema, including window functions
Has defined metrics in a semantic layer or a BI calculation language

Setup: a laptop CPU with uv, or Google Colab. Nothing downloads a model; the assistant labs replay recorded replies of a scripted stand-in model, and a free hosted model is optional. Run 00_setup_check before Day 1; see labs/README.md.

outcomes.text: Design a semantic layer with entities, grain, conformed time and governed metrics for several business areas, given the company's marts, a tariff history and Hijri and fiscal calendars
outcomes.evidence: model files whose reconciliation tests pass against source totals

outcomes.text: Implement metric definitions as code with owners, tests and change control, given three conflicting definitions of the collection rate
outcomes.evidence: metric files and one change taken through review in continuous integration

outcomes.text: Configure row-level access and field masking in the semantic layer according to data classification, given three user roles and the national classification levels
outcomes.evidence: access tests that pass for each role and catch a seeded leak

outcomes.text: Evaluate a conversational assistant on certified questions, measuring accuracy, stability, wrong but plausible answers and the contribution of each kind of semantic context, given 60 bilingual questions with certified answers and a fixed model
outcomes.evidence: a report from a harness a reviewer can re-run

outcomes.text: Decide which question types the assistant may answer and under which safeguards, given the evaluation results and a stated tolerance for wrong figures
outcomes.evidence: a routing policy with a decision record

outcomes.text: Review the design of a peer's analytics product for correctness, portability and governance, given a peer's semantic model and evaluation
outcomes.evidence: design review notes with findings ranked by risk

case_study.name: Qamar Telecom
case_study.summary: Qamar Telecom is a fictional Saudi telecom operator whose 300 managers want to ask, in Arabic and English, about usage, billing, collections and complaints, while finance, collections and customer care each report a different collection rate. Participants certify one collection rate, write the metrics as tested code with owners and change control, build a conformed semantic layer with tariff history, fiscal and Hijri calendars and access rules by region and classification, export it to an open format, serve it to tools and agents, and evaluate Daleel, the bilingual assistant, on 60 certified questions before deciding which questions it may answer. All data is synthetic and generated with a fixed seed.

format_note: Intensive: 4 teaching days of four sessions and a capstone day, with guided pre-work and a tracked follow-up task

days.title: Capstone: a governed analytics product and its design review

capstone.summary: A governed analytics product for two business areas (metrics as code, a semantic layer with tested access rules, an assistant evaluation on at least 40 certified questions, a routing policy) in a public repository whose README reports measured accuracy and stability, defended in a design review
capstone.submission: A public GitHub repository for two business areas of Qamar Telecom: metric files with tests and the review rules in continuous integration, the semantic model with access rules and their tests, an evaluation of the assistant on at least 40 certified questions (accuracy, wrong but plausible answers, stability over three runs) from a harness a reviewer can re-run, and a routing policy with its decision record; the README reports the measured accuracy and stability. Then a live design review in which the participant re-runs the evaluation on five questions the assessor adds.
